question.prompt: In a particular game, each of \(4\) players rolls a standard \(6\)-sided die. The winner is the player who rolls the highest number. If there is a tie for the highest roll, those involved in the tie will roll again and this process will continue until one player wins. Hugo is one of the players in this game. What is the probability that Hugo’s first roll was a \(5,\) given that he won the game?

solutions.title: Use the highest first roll
solutions.explanation:
The eventual winner must have been among the players tied for the highest first roll. Thus the winner’s first number is exactly the maximum of the four first rolls.

Let \(M\) be that maximum, and let \(W\) be the event that Hugo wins. All four players have the same chance of winning, so \(P(W)=\frac14\).

The same symmetry holds when we consider only games with \(M=5\). This restriction does not favor any player: swapping the players’ names preserves both the restriction and the rules. Therefore,
\[
P(W\mid M=5)=\frac14.
\]
When Hugo wins, his first roll is \(5\) exactly when \(M=5\). Consequently, the requested conditional probability is
\[
\frac{P(M=5\text{ and }W)}{P(W)}
=\frac{P(M=5)\cdot\frac14}{\frac14}
=P(M=5).
\]

There are \(6^4\) equally likely ordered outcomes for the four first rolls. Of these, \(5^4\) have every roll at most \(5\), and \(4^4\) have every roll at most \(4\). Subtracting leaves precisely those whose maximum is \(5\). Hence the answer is
\[
\frac{5^4-4^4}{6^4}
=\frac{625-256}{1296}
=\boxed{\frac{41}{144}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

solutions.title: Count the possible ties
solutions.explanation:
If Hugo first rolls \(5\), he can win only if nobody rolls \(6\). We can therefore count according to how many opponents also roll \(5\).

If exactly \(t\) opponents tie Hugo, the remaining \(t+1\) players have equal chances in the rerolling process. Hugo’s probability of eventually winning is \(\frac1{t+1}\), even if further ties occur.

There are \(6^4\) equally likely ordered first-round outcomes. With Hugo’s roll fixed at \(5\), the relevant outcomes are counted below.

| Opponents rolling \(5\) | Number of first-round outcomes | Hugo’s eventual winning probability |
|---|---:|---:|
| \(0\) | \(4^3=64\) | \(1\) |
| \(1\) | \(3\cdot4^2=48\) | \(\frac12\) |
| \(2\) | \(3\cdot4=12\) | \(\frac13\) |
| \(3\) | \(1\) | \(\frac14\) |

For each row, choose which opponents roll \(5\); every other opponent has four choices, \(1\) through \(4\). These cases are disjoint and cover every first round in which Hugo rolls \(5\) and can still win.

Weighting each case by Hugo’s winning probability gives
\[
P(\text{Hugo first rolls }5\text{ and wins})
=\frac{64+48\left(\frac12\right)+12\left(\frac13\right)+\frac14}{6^4}
=\frac{369}{5184}.
\]
By symmetry, Hugo wins the game with probability \(\frac14\). Conditional probability therefore gives
\[
P(\text{Hugo first rolls }5\mid\text{Hugo wins})
=\frac{369/5184}{1/4}
=\boxed{\frac{41}{144}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
